topic: 限时写作：立场与充分论证 · Independent new scenario: a lecture examining unintended policy consequences
grammarFocus: 让步、条件、因果；复杂句和简单句的清楚组合。 Teach the new rule in Chinese, then provide at least 8 distinct grammar questions in new sentences. Distinguish a newly taught form from revision. All main reading/listening question prompts and options must be English, with short A0/A1 English prompts. Chinese explanations are allowed. Preserve a coherent new scenario; do not rename an earlier text, reuse its facts or reveal answers in question stems.
sourcePolicy: Project-original scenario; simulated figures and people; no copied official test, textbook, GitHub PDF or third-party audio.
title: The Ripple Effect: When Well-Meant Rules Backfire
instructions: 本材料为模拟教学练习，并非官方雅思考试。请先听/读英文讲座，理解政策意外后果的逻辑。然后完成10道听力/阅读题（单选、填空、匹配、判断）。之后学习语法点“让步、条件、因果的清晰组合”，并完成8道新句语法题。最后进行口语和写作迁移练习。所有题目选项为英文，解释为中文。
transcript:
Professor Lin: Good morning, everyone. Today we look at unintended policy consequences. Let me start with a small example. A city council wanted to reduce traffic downtown. So they built a new ring road around the city center. The road was wide and fast. Drivers loved it. But within two years, traffic downtown increased by fifteen percent. Why? Because the new road made driving into the city easier. More people decided to drive. This is called induced demand. Although the council built the road to reduce traffic, it actually attracted more cars. 

Student A: Professor, does that mean we should never build new roads? 

Professor Lin: Not exactly. We need to think about conditions. If a city builds new roads but also improves public transport, then the result may be different. The key is to combine policies. 

Student B: I read about a similar case with plastic bags. A government banned free plastic bags in supermarkets. Shoppers had to pay for them. At first, plastic bag use dropped by eighty percent. But then people started buying thicker, reusable bags. Those bags were made of more plastic. So total plastic production went up. The policy reduced one problem but created another. 

Professor Lin: Excellent example. This shows a trade-off. When you make one behavior costly, people may switch to another behavior that is also harmful. 

Student C: What about the tax on sugary drinks? Some cities tried that. 

Professor Lin: Yes. A tax on sugary drinks can reduce consumption. However, if the tax is too high, people may buy cheaper, unhealthy alternatives, like energy drinks with even more sugar. So the effect depends on how people respond. 

Student A: So policies always have side effects? 

Professor Lin: Almost always. But we can predict some of them. We use models. A model is a simplified picture of reality. It helps us ask: if we do X, what else might happen? For example, a rent control policy sets a maximum rent. It helps current tenants pay less. But if landlords cannot earn enough, they may stop renting out apartments. Then the supply of housing falls. In the long run, rent control can make housing harder to find. 

Student B: That sounds unfair. 

Professor Lin: It is a dilemma. The policy helps some people now but may hurt others later. Good policy design tries to balance short-term help with long-term effects. 

Student C: How do we know if a policy worked? 

Professor Lin: We compare what happened with what would have happened without the policy. That is called a counterfactual. It is hard because we cannot see the alternative world. But we can use data from similar cities. 

Student A: So the main lesson is to think carefully before we act? 

Professor Lin: Yes. And to monitor results after we act. Policies are experiments. We must be ready to adjust them. 

Student B: Thank you, Professor. This was very clear. 

Professor Lin: You're welcome. Next week we will discuss how to communicate policy changes to the public.

The price of sugary drinks may fall

grammar.title: 让步、条件、因果的清晰组合
grammar.explanation: 在英语中，我们常用连词来表达逻辑关系。让步：although / even though / though，表示“虽然”，后面跟一个事实，主句给出相反或意外的结果。条件：if / unless，表示“如果/除非”，提出一个条件，主句说明结果。因果：because / so / therefore，表示原因或结果。复杂句可以组合这些关系，但要注意句子不要过长，简单句和复杂句交替使用，让意思清楚。例如：Although the council built the road to reduce traffic, it actually attracted more cars. 这里 although 引导让步，主句用 actually 强调意外结果。再如：If a city builds new roads but also improves public transport, then the result may be different. 这里 if 引导条件，then 引出结果。
grammar.example: Although the council built the road to reduce traffic, it actually attracted more cars.

questions.prompt: _____ the weather was cold, many people went to the beach.
questions.explanation: 前后是让步关系：虽然天气冷，但很多人去海滩。Although 表示“虽然”。
questions.evidence: Although the council built the road to reduce traffic, it actually attracted more cars.

questions.prompt: You will miss the bus _____ you leave now.
questions.explanation: 句意：除非你现在离开，否则你会错过公交车。unless 表示“除非”。
questions.evidence: If a city builds new roads but also improves public transport, then the result may be different.

questions.prompt: The company lost money _____ the manager made poor decisions.
questions.explanation: 经理决策失误是公司亏损的原因，用 because 引导原因。
questions.evidence: Because the new road made driving into the city easier.

questions.prompt: She studied hard, _____ she passed the exam.
questions.explanation: 她努力学习，因此通过了考试。so 表示结果。
questions.evidence: So total plastic production went up.

questions.explanation: 加热冰，冰会融化，这是条件关系，用 If。
questions.evidence: If a city builds new roads but also improves public transport, then the result may be different.

questions.prompt: He didn't buy the car _____ it was too expensive.
questions.explanation: 车太贵是他不买的原因，用 because。
questions.evidence: Because the new road made driving into the city easier.

questions.prompt: _____ it was raining, they played football outside.
questions.explanation: 虽然下雨，他们仍在外面踢足球，让步关系用 Even though。
questions.evidence: Although the council built the road to reduce traffic, it actually attracted more cars.

questions.prompt: You won't improve _____ you practice every day.
questions.explanation: 除非每天练习，否则不会提高。unless 表示“除非”。
questions.evidence: If a city builds new roads but also improves public transport, then the result may be different.
